correctness.rationale: Hall inequalities are necessary and sufficient for covering all three plants with distinct surviving pollinators. Every graph in the finite class corresponds to one sorted sequence of seven possible nonempty neighborhood masks; standard-library integer enumeration exhausts each sequence, every one-edge addition, and every survivor subset, and certifies uniform coefficientwise dominance for \(n\le6\). At \(n=7\) exactly 24 exceptions have listed gain vectors, forcing the exact switch thresholds 1/2 or 2/3; independent direct assignment enumeration checks every witness survivor case. Symbolic polynomials, not numerical sampling, establish all real-p comparisons. No claim for \(n>7\).

originality.rationale: Exact new claim classifies probability-dependent optimal one-incidence augmentations of fixed connected three-plant matchable networks under independent right-vertex failure, including the sharp seven-pollinator boundary. The full-text matching-augmentation precursor Hommelsheim et al. concerns adversarial deletion of one existing edge, not arbitrary independent node survival or a probability ranking of one added link. Dietzfelbinger--Rink study the distribution of randomly generated bipartite graphs with optimized degrees, not link augmentation of a fixed graph. Pollination papers frame robustness and rewiring but do not imply the capacity-one matching augmentation threshold. General node-connectivity reliability does not dominate matching-service reliability. Historical priority not independently certified.
residual_risks: There may be prior matching reliability-polynomial or stochastic graph-augmentation classifications under other names, not located by these searches.
Complete texts of Kaiser-Bunbury (2010) and Goldschmidt et al. (1994) were not accessible and are assessed only within abstract scope.

value.rationale: Simultaneous unit-capacity pollinator service is a distinct, naturally motivated limited-resource objective for interaction protection. A fixed budget of one added interaction yields a complete small-guild boundary where best policy first depends on survival probability, with 24 exceptional incidence structures and two exact rational thresholds. This is a sharp, nontrivial matching-reliability classification, not a renamed scalar expectation. Interpretation remains theoretical and should not be treated as empirical management guidance.
